name: Home Assistant
description: Open source home automation that puts local control and privacy first.
summary: Home Assistant's Open Home Foundation AI policy permits AI assistance across code, documentation, issues, and comments, but requires human understanding, review, and accountability, and bans autonomous agents. Some repositories also require contributors to answer AI-use questions in pull request templates.

evidence.quote: AI can be a helpful tool to write code and documentation. But our projects are open source foundations that many people build on, so we require a human in the loop who understands the work the AI produced.
Review and understand every contribution before you submit it. You should be able to explain every change in your pull request.
We don't allow autonomous agents to contribute to our projects. We close pull requests and issues that we believe were created autonomously, and we may mark automated comments as spam.
Several repositories ask about AI in their pull request template. Leave those parts in place, and answer them honestly.
You can use AI tools to help you write. But don't let a tool post content on your behalf that you haven't reviewed.
Autonomous agents are not allowed. Pull requests and issues created by them are closed.
You are responsible for everything you submit. You must understand it, and be able to explain every change in your own words.
You can use AI tools to help you write. But don't let a tool post content on your behalf that you haven't reviewed.
If AI helped you write the description, check it for technical accuracy.
Using AI to improve grammar or clarity is fine, but the substance of your answers must be your own.
Several repositories ask about AI in their pull request template. Leave those parts in place, and answer them honestly.
